The comparison examines the number and proportion of incident patients with atrial fibrillation seen by [[praktiserende-kardiologer|Praktiserende kardiologer]] across the five Danish regions during the annual report period. The data reveals a stark regional inequality in patient distribution and incidence rates, with a massive concentration of cases in the capital area.

[[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] is the clear leader, accounting for the vast majority of incident patients. It reported 790 patients, which corresponds to an incidence proportion of 12.7% [^src1]. This makes it a significant outlier, as its proportion is nearly three times the national average of 4.8% [^src1]. In contrast, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] is the absolute trailer, reporting exactly zero incident patients (0.0%) during the same period [^src1].

The remaining regions fall well below the capital's numbers but show varying levels of activity. [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] reported 95 patients (3.9%), [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] recorded 113 patients (2.2%), and [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] had the lowest non-zero count with 66 patients (1.9%) [^src1]. Nationally, the total number of incident patients across all regions was 1064, with an overall proportion of 4.8% [^src1]. Because this analysis is based on a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends can be established regarding whether these regional disparities are widening or narrowing over time.

- "Region Sjælland har iværksat en intern undersøgelse af registrerings- og dataflow-fejl i forbindelse med indikator 8" — see [[quality-improvement-action|Quality Improvement Action]] ([[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland — Sjælland]]) [^src27]
